quickstart.title: Quickstart
quickstart.description: Download SKIA Forge, sign in, and run your first governed workflow in the desktop IDE.

step-by-step.title: Step-by-Step
step-by-step.html:
01
Download SKIA Forge from forge.skia.ca/platform-downloads for your operating system.
02
Install the app, then open SKIA Forge from your applications menu or desktop shortcut.
03
Sign in with your SKIA account or create one when prompted � authentication happens inside the application.
04
Open or import a project, submit work, review governance output, and apply changes when you are ready.
05
Explore deeper guides from the links below when you need more detail.

next-steps.title: Next Steps
next-steps.html:
User Guide � day-to-day usage and governance modes
API Reference � HTTP APIs for developers and automation
Product Manual � capabilities overview
Support � how to get help

user-guide.title: User Guide
user-guide.description: What SKIA Forge does for you, how to install and sign in, daily workflows, governance modes in plain language, and where to get help.

what-skia-forge-does-for-you.title: What SKIA Forge Does For You
what-skia-forge-does-for-you.html: SKIA Forge helps you build software with AI assistance under clear governance: planning, reviews, architecture insight, and safer apply paths so your team can move fast without bypassing policy.

get-the-desktop-ide.title: Get the Desktop IDE
get-the-desktop-ide.html: Download installers from forge.skia.ca/platform-downloads and install SKIA Forge for your platform.

signing-in.title: Signing In
signing-in.html: Open the app and sign in or create a SKIA account when prompted. Authentication happens inside the application.

daily-usage.title: Daily Usage
daily-usage.html:
01
Open or import the project you want to work on.
02
Submit work and review governance output before applying changes.
03
Follow in-app remediation when something is blocked, then try again.

governance-modes.title: Governance Modes
governance-modes.html:
Strict � safest default; more steps require explicit approval.
Adaptive � balanced; routine work flows faster while higher-risk actions surface for review.
Autonomous � fastest path where enabled; use when your team accepts the trade-offs.

Labels in the product may vary; ask your admin which mode applies to your workspace.

where-to-get-help.title: Where to Get Help
where-to-get-help.html:
Support and Troubleshooting
Contact & Support on the Forge site for routed requests

developer-guide.title: Developer Guide
developer-guide.description: Local setup, project structure, coding conventions, and integration notes.

local-setup.title: Local Setup
local-setup.html:
01
Ensure Node.js 20+ is installed
02
npm install
03
npm run build
04
npm run test

project-structure.title: Project Structure
project-structure.html:
the Forge server � runtime entrypoint
src/forge/modules/ � module domains: governance, safety, context-engine, agent, production, healing, architecture
SKIA Forge IDE � IDE-facing integration surface
docs/ � product documentation set
public/ � static assets and HTML pages

development-workflow.title: Development Workflow
development-workflow.html:
01
Implement scoped changes in src/forge/modules/*.
02
Run npm run lint, npm run typecheck, npm run test.
03
Validate integration routes and control-plane behaviour.

coding-conventions.title: Coding Conventions
coding-conventions.html:
Use typed request/response schemas for all API surfaces
Keep policy checks explicit and test-covered
Prefer additive changes over implicit behaviour changes

integration-notes.title: Integration Notes
integration-notes.html: Forge can run with SKIA integration enabled or disabled. Adapter paths should fail clearly and return structured errors when upstream contracts are unavailable.

api-reference.title: API Reference
api-reference.description: Forge HTTP API as implemented in the Forge server. Authenticated clients are required for control-plane routes under /api/forge/* . For the complete route index see docs/API_REFERENCE.md in the repository.

auth-proxy.html:

rpc.title: RPC
rpc.html: POST /rpc � SKIA-backed operations with local fallbacks for unavailable upstream paths

error-model.title: Error Model
error-model.html:
Schema validation errors return structured request feedback with field-level detail
Upstream unavailability returns explicit SKIA unavailable errors
Governance blocks return mode and policy-based decision context with remediation guidance

operator-manual.title: Operator Manual
operator-manual.description: Deployment baseline, operational checks, and incident handling for SKIA Forge.

runtime-role.title: Runtime Role
runtime-role.html: SKIA Forge operates as an orchestration and governance runtime service that augments development workflows with policy-aware controls.

deployment-baseline.title: Deployment Baseline
deployment-baseline.html:
Production hostname: forge.skia.ca. Release baseline Forge 1.0.0 and SKIA Forge IDE 1.0.0.

01
npm run build
02
npm run dev
(or your production process command)
03
Listen on SKIA_PORT (default 4173). Validate /health, /live, /ready, /version

Additional environment variables for signing and GitHub integration are documented in your onboarding package.

environment-secrets.title: Environment & Secrets
environment-secrets.html:
Keep all secrets in environment management � never commit credentials
Configure SKIA integration values per deployment environment via your hosting provider's environment variables
Use explicit mode controls for strict vs adaptive operations

operational-checks.title: Operational Checks
operational-checks.html:
Health checks pass: /health returns 200 ok
Control-plane posture shows expected governance mode
Governance recommendations are readable and actionable
Audit logs are being produced after orchestration runs

incident-handling.title: Incident Handling
incident-handling.html:
01
Capture failure endpoint and payload metadata.
02
Review control-plane recommendations from /api/forge/control-plane.
03
Apply remediation and re-run the failed request.
04
Escalate with logs and request IDs if unresolved � contact support.

product-manual.title: Product Manual
product-manual.description: The governance and orchestration control plane for AI-native software development. SKIA Forge connects to SKIA intelligence services for orchestration; it does not replace the full SKIA product runtime.

what-skia-forge-is.title: What SKIA Forge Is
what-skia-forge-is.html: SKIA Forge coordinates planning, execution safety, architecture checks, and remediation guidance around AI-assisted workflows.

delivery-surfaces.title: Delivery Surfaces
delivery-surfaces.html: Public download and documentation live at forge.skia.ca, including /platform-downloads, /resources, /security, /contact, and /docs/*. The web IDE is available at /forge/app when the IDE bundle is built. Account sign-in and registration happen in the SKIA Forge IDE or other supported clients, not on static marketing pages. Desktop installers are served via /api/app/download routes.

who-it-is-for.title: Who It Is For
who-it-is-for.html:
AI-First Engineering Teams
Build faster with safety guardrails baked into every workflow.
Platform & Productivity Teams
Governance-aware automation for platform-level development workflows.
Security & Governance Stakeholders
Policy-aware automation that produces first-class audit trails.

core-capabilities.title: Core Capabilities
core-capabilities.html:
Structured orchestration across context, agent, SDLC, production, healing, architecture, and related modules
Governance mode controls: strict, adaptive, autonomous
Runtime control-plane posture, alerts, and recommendations
Safety and architecture diagnostics on changed files
Integration with SKIA intelligence services for reasoning and execution support

value-proposition.title: Value Proposition
value-proposition.html:
Faster delivery with guardrails � ship confidently without sacrificing speed
Reduced unsafe operations reaching production
Better traceability for enterprise governance and audits

product-boundaries.title: Product Boundaries
product-boundaries.html: SKIA Forge is a control and orchestration layer. It is not a replacement for your full application runtime � it integrates with upstream SKIA intelligence contracts and your existing deployment topology.

security-guide.title: Security Guide
security-guide.description: Layered controls, key components, operational practices, and hardening checklist.

security-model.title: Security Model
security-model.html:
Request Validation
All inputs validated against strict schemas before execution.
Governance Enforcement
Strict, adaptive, and autonomous modes control agent permissions.
Safety Gates
High-risk actions pass through safety gates with execution previews.
Policy-Based Blocking
Policy violations are blocked, logged, and returned with remediation.

authentication-accounts.title: Authentication & Accounts
authentication-accounts.html:
All Forge API routes require authentication. Sign in via the SKIA Forge IDE or your API client.
Marketing HTML omits web sign-in/register CTAs; users authenticate in the SKIA Forge IDE.

key-security-components.title: Key Security Components
key-security-components.html:
SecurityAnalysisService � scan and save-time checks on code and agent output
Governance decision engine � strict / adaptive / autonomous control with audit trail
Route and action-level safety modules � per-surface constraints that cannot be bypassed

operational-security-practices.title: Operational Security Practices
operational-security-practices.html:
Keep secrets out of repositories and logs � use your hosting provider's environment variables
Validate all external integration responses � never trust third-party data without assertion
Treat policy blocks as first-class security events � every block is logged and reviewable
Record and monitor remediation outcomes � fixes without validation are incomplete

hardening-checklist.title: Hardening Checklist
hardening-checklist.html:
Run lint, typecheck, and tests before every release
Keep all dependencies current
Validate integration probe endpoints regularly
Review audit trails after major orchestration runs
Rotate JWT_SECRET and API keys on schedule
Never commit secrets � use environment injection

troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting
troubleshooting.description: Diagnostics and step-by-step fixes for the most common SKIA Forge issues.

build-test-failures.title: Build / Test Failures
build-test-failures.html:
01
npm run typecheck
02
npm run test
03
npm run build
04
Fix schema and type mismatches before re-running orchestration endpoints.

skia-integration-unavailable.title: SKIA Integration Unavailable
skia-integration-unavailable.html:
01
Check /integration/skia-full and /integration/skia-full/probe.
02
Verify upstream URL and environment configuration in your hosting provider.
03
Review adapter disabled flags and auth headers.

governance-blocks.title: Governance Blocks
governance-blocks.html:
Expected in strict or adaptive mode for risky actions
Read remediation recommendations from the block response
Apply the suggested safe path and re-run the request

runtime-health-issues.title: Runtime Health Issues
runtime-health-issues.html:
01
Validate /health and /live endpoints.
02
Check logs for failing module names and request IDs.
03
Isolate whether the issue is a local Forge module or an upstream contract failure.
04
If unresolved, escalate via Contact & Support with request ID and logs.

changelog.title: Changelog
changelog.description: Notable changes to SKIA Forge, documented by release.

v1-0-0-initial-release.title: v1.0.0 — Initial release
v1-0-0-initial-release.html:
SKIA Forge control plane with governance modes, orchestration APIs, and integration with SKIA intelligence services.
SKIA Forge IDE (desktop) and web shell at /forge/app for browser-based access.
Public documentation, security guide, support model, and download hub at forge.skia.ca.

support.title: Support
support.description: SKIA Forge support covers the following areas:

support-scope.title: Support Scope
support-scope.html:
Runtime startup and health issues
Integration contract failures
Governance and policy flow debugging
Build and test pipeline breakages

triage-information-to-collect.title: Triage Information to Collect
triage-information-to-collect.html:
Endpoint and HTTP method
Request timestamp
Request ID or correlation ID (if available)
What you were trying to do when the issue occurred
Full error message and reproduction steps

escalation-path.title: Escalation Path
escalation-path.html:
01
Reproduce locally and validate with /health and probe endpoints.
02
Apply remediation guidance from control-plane outputs.
03
Escalate with logs, payload shape, and expected vs actual behaviour.

enterprise-support-expectations.title: Enterprise Support Expectations
enterprise-support-expectations.html:
P1
Critical Outage
Immediate response window.
P2
Degraded Service
Same business day response.
P3
Non-blocking Issue
Prioritized backlog response.

pricing-and-packages.title: Pricing & Packages
pricing-and-packages.description: SKIA Forge is available in three packages designed for individuals, teams, and enterprise organisations.

packages.html:

Solo engineers & experiments

optional-add-ons.title: Optional Add-ons
optional-add-ons.html:
Custom policy packs
Integration acceleration services
Architecture and security review workshops
Rollout training for platform and security teams

enterprise-readiness-checklist.title: Enterprise Readiness Checklist
enterprise-readiness-checklist.description: Your guide to evaluating and deploying SKIA Forge at scale. Use this checklist when your organisation is deciding whether SKIA Forge fits your engineering, security, and operations requirements.

product-architecture.title: Product & Architecture
product-architecture.html:
Your team should confirm the product scope matches your expectations: governance and orchestration for AI-assisted development, aligned with your delivery stack.
Your team should confirm you have a clear picture of core capabilities from the product manual and public materials.
Your team should confirm integration expectations with your existing tools and workflows are documented internally.
Your team should confirm you have access to an up-to-date API reference for any automation or custom clients.

security-governance.title: Security & Governance
security-governance.html:
Your team should confirm security controls and threat assumptions are acceptable under your policies (Security Guide).
Your team should confirm how governance modes map to your risk appetite and who can change them.
Your team should confirm high-risk operations, approvals, and audit expectations meet compliance needs.
Your team should confirm secret handling and access control for Forge hosts match your standards.

operations.title: Operations
operations.html:
Your team should confirm you have an operational runbook for deployment, upgrades, and rollback (Operator Manual).
Your team should confirm health and readiness checks you rely on are defined and monitored.
Your team should confirm troubleshooting and escalation paths are understood (Support, Troubleshooting).
Your team should confirm backup, recovery, and incident response procedures are assigned.

quality-reliability.title: Quality & Reliability
quality-reliability.html:
Your team should confirm release quality expectations align with your internal gates.
Your team should confirm known limitations and non-goals are captured for stakeholders.
Your team should confirm performance and availability targets for your topology are documented.

commercial-support.title: Commercial & Support
commercial-support.html:
Your team should confirm packaging and licensing match the seats or deployment model you intend (Pricing & Packages).
Your team should confirm support tiers and escalation contacts are agreed with SKIA.
Your team should confirm procurement items (security questionnaires, DPA, subprocessors if applicable) are tracked before go-live.
